summary: Backend Engineer with 6+ years of experience building backend and event-driven systems with Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch, and AWS. Currently working on financial reporting workflows supporting regulatory reporting, with a focus on backend services, data validation, asynchronous processing, and reliability. Previously built document processing and CDC-based search systems handling high-volume data. Comfortable working across application code, messaging, databases, testing, and observability.

bullets: Enhanced backend services for a financial reporting platform supporting regulatory reporting workflows. Developed Java/Spring Boot components for data validation, mapping, consolidation, and report generation across multiple services, with reporting cycles handling 50K+ records.
Worked on Kafka-based processing between reporting services, adding retry and dead-letter handling for failed messages and making consumers idempotent so duplicate events could be processed safely.

Developed configurable validation and mapping components covering 20+ business rules for data-quality checks, missing fields, and invalid values, reducing manual validation effort by 30% across test datasets.

Enhanced report approval workflows with state-based transitions, optimistic locking, and audit logging. This helped prevent conflicting updates when reports were reviewed concurrently and provided traceability across the reporting lifecycle.

Improved processing performance by 20% in load-test scenarios involving 100K+ records by tuning database queries, increasing Kafka consumer parallelism, and introducing Redis caching where repeated lookups were involved.

Added OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and Grafana instrumentation for API latency, processing failures, distributed traces, and Kafka consumer lag. Also expanded automated tests with JUnit 5, Mockito, and Testcontainers, reaching 85% coverage across owned components.

Built Spring Boot microservices for an internal document processing platform handling 5,000+ scanned PDFs/images per day. Kafka was used to decouple processing stages, while AWS Textract, S3, Lambda, and EventBridge handled OCR, storage, and asynchronous processing. Reduced manual processing time by 80%.

Replaced SQL-based text search with Elasticsearch and built a CDC pipeline using Debezium, Kafka Connect, and Kafka Streams to synchronize 2M+ PostgreSQL records with the search index. Updates reached Elasticsearch in under 5 minutes, while search latency improved by 70%.

Built an event-driven feedback routing workflow using Kafka, AWS Lambda, and EventBridge, integrating lightweight NLP models for automated classification and routing. Reduced manual routing effort by 60% while maintaining 90%+ classification accuracy.
